caption: The drawing depicts two textile objects on a plain background. The larger textile fragment, occupying the lower left and center, is irregularly shaped and predominantly consists of two colors: a deep indigo blue and a faded beige or off-white. The pattern on this textile is composed of various floral motifs, including large flowers such as roses and intricate leafy designs, all rendered in alternating light and dark areas with sharp contrast between the indigo and beige portions. The fabric appears divided into sections—some feature prominent flowers, another section has geometric forms, and others show interlaced foliage and decorative borders. The texture of the weave is visible, and vertical, parallel lines run through the fabric, indicating either the weave structure or wear. In the upper right corner, a smaller rectangular fragment is displayed, also featuring a floral and possibly a geometric motif, with the same indigo and beige color palette. The smaller piece includes a central band of floral medallions framed by narrow borders with more detailed, possibly vine-like patterns. At the bottom left of the drawing, the name "Elmar Weise" is inscribed in simple, uppercase letters.
title: Handwoven Tapestry Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
